title: Homocysteine-lowering interventions for preventing cardiovascular events
authors: Martí-Carvajal AJ, Solà I, Lathyris D, Dayer M
population: 15 randomised trials of vitamin B6, B9 or B12 supplements in people with or without cardiovascular disease
funder: Internal sources: no sources of support provided. External sources: Iberoamerican Cochrane Centre, Spain (academic); Cochrane Heart Group, UK (academic).
authorConflicts: A.J. Martí-Carvajal was paid by Eli Lilly in 2004 and by Merck in 2007 to run workshops on appraising clinical trials, stated as unrelated to Cochrane work; no interests known for the other authors.
result: 15 RCTs, 71,422 participants, follow-up 1 to 7.3 years. Against placebo, homocysteine-lowering interventions showed no difference in myocardial infarction (7.1% against 6.0%; RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.95-1.10; 12 trials, 46,699 participants), death from any cause (11.7% against 12.3%; RR 1.01, 0.96-1.06; 11 trials, 44,817) or serious adverse events (8.3% against 8.5%; RR 1.07, 1.00-1.14), and were associated with reduced stroke (4.3% against 5.1%; RR 0.90, 0.82-0.99; 10 trials, 44,224). Background: normal total homocysteine is close to 10 umol/L; fasting 12-30 umol/L is termed mild or moderate, 31-100 intermediate and above 100 severe hyperhomocysteinaemia.
